prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

EL PASO, Texas (CNN) -- CNN Hero Maria Ruiz has been changing the lives of children and their families in Juarez, Mexico, for more than 12 years. But lately, it's been Ruiz's own life that's been changing. Crews prepare to demolish Maria Ruiz's home as part of ABC's "Extreme Makeover: Home Edition." In November, "CNN Heroes: An All-Star Tribute" honored Ruiz for crossing the Texas border to Juarez several times a week to deliver food, clothing and toys to impoverished children and their families. Months later, Ruiz and her family received another surprise, courtesy of ABC's "Extreme Makeover: Home Edition." Ruiz, her husband and their two children were sent on a five-day vacation to the Bahamas while thousands of volunteers built the family a custom-designed home. "When Ty Pennington came to our home and said, 'Ruiz family, come on out,' we all just ran out and couldn't believe that we were chosen," Ruiz said. "It's a blessing to us, but we weren't expecting all of this at all, and it has been overwhelming." Pennington is the host of "Extreme Makeover: Home Edition," which selected Ruiz and her family from thousands of applicants throughout Texas. Pennington said the idea was to give Ruiz what she needed most: the tools to do more.  Watch Ruiz and her family react to their new home » . In addition to bringing supplies to the people of Juarez, Ruiz and her family are completing construction of a complex there, which includes a community kitchen, an orphanage and a trade school. Read more about Ruiz's work . In order to devote their time to the Juarez community, the family put construction of their own home on hold in 1996, Ruiz said, leaving many parts unfinished. They were also using much of their living space as a warehouse for all of the donations for the Juarez families, she said. "A home is somewhere you can go after a long day's work and relax and where the family can get together and be able to sit down and talk about our day," Ruiz said. "When we had the things in the living room, we couldn't do that there." Upon returning from the Bahamas, Ruiz and her family were surrounded by thousands of volunteers and community members who blocked them from seeing the changes by the show's large bus. After chanting the show's coined phrase -- "Move that bus!" -- Ruiz and her family were introduced to their new home. "For us, it is a new beginning, and it's going to change our lives," Ruiz said. With her new home, Ruiz will be able to continue -- and even expand -- her family's work for those in need. According to Executive Producer Anthony Dominici, both an additional kitchen and storage space were built in the new home for Ruiz. And "through the generosity of the community," enough donations of food, clothes and toys were collected to fill a 20-foot shipping container and a 16-foot cube truck -- including more than 75,000 cans of food, Dominici said. "That's the whole point here," Pennington said. "To give her what she needs to make her life easier to literally spread dreams and hope to people who have absolutely none of either one of those." For Ruiz, it's about teaching young minds so they can in turn give back to their community. "If you teach them and train them as a child and they go out and do the same, we would live in a much better world." "CNN Heroes: An All-Star Tribute" introduced Ruiz to the world when it premiered on Thanksgiving on the global networks of CNN. Actress Selena Gomez introduced and presented Ruiz with her CNN Hero award. Each of the top 10 CNN Heroes also received $25,000.  Watch Ruiz accept her CNN Hero Award » . Nominations for 2009 CNN Heroes opened January 1 and can be submitted at www.CNN.com/Heroes. The Ruiz family episode of "Extreme Makeover: Home Edition" is scheduled to air March 15.

outputs.L1:
**EL PASO, Texas (CNN) —** For more than 12 years, CNN Hero Maria Ruiz has been transforming the lives of children and families in Juarez, Mexico. Lately, however, Ruiz’s own life has been undergoing a transformation.

Crews prepared to demolish Ruiz’s home as part of ABC’s “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition.”

In November, “CNN Heroes: An All-Star Tribute” honored Ruiz for crossing the Texas border into Juarez several times a week to deliver food, clothing and toys to impoverished children and their families.

Months later, Ruiz and her family received another surprise, courtesy of ABC’s “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition.” Ruiz, her husband and their two children were sent on a five-day vacation to the Bahamas while thousands of volunteers built them a custom-designed home.

“When Ty Pennington came to our home and said, ‘Ruiz family, come on out,’ we all just ran out and couldn’t believe that we were chosen,” Ruiz said. “It’s a blessing to us, but we weren’t expecting all of this at all, and it has been overwhelming.”

Pennington, the host of “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition,” said the show selected Ruiz and her family from among thousands of applicants across Texas. He said the goal was to give Ruiz what she needed most: the tools to do more.

**Watch Ruiz and her family react to their new home »**

In addition to delivering supplies to the people of Juarez, Ruiz and her family are completing construction of a complex there that includes a community kitchen, an orphanage and a trade school.

**Read more about Ruiz’s work »**

To devote more time to the Juarez community, the family put construction of their own home on hold in 1996, Ruiz said, leaving many areas unfinished. They also used much of their living space as a warehouse for donations intended for families in Juarez.

“A home is somewhere you can go after a long day’s work and relax and where the family can get together and be able to sit down and talk about our day,” Ruiz said. “When we had the things in the living room, we couldn’t do that there.”

When Ruiz and her family returned from the Bahamas, thousands of volunteers and community members surrounded them as the show’s large bus blocked their view of the changes. After the crowd chanted the show’s signature phrase — “Move that bus!” — Ruiz and her family were introduced to their new home.

“For us, it is a new beginning, and it’s going to change our lives,” Ruiz said.

With her new home, Ruiz will be able to continue — and even expand — her family’s work on behalf of those in need. According to executive producer Anthony Dominici, the new home includes an additional kitchen and storage space for Ruiz.

And “through the generosity of the community,” enough donations of food, clothing and toys were collected to fill a 20-foot shipping container and a 16-foot cube truck — including more than 75,000 cans of food, Dominici said.

“That’s the whole point here,” Pennington said. “To give her what she needs to make her life easier, to literally spread dreams and hope to people who have absolutely none of either one of those.”

For Ruiz, the mission is about educating young minds so they can, in turn, give back to their community.

“If you teach them and train them as a child and they go out and do the same, we would live in a much better world.”

“CNN Heroes: An All-Star Tribute” introduced Ruiz to the world when it premiered on Thanksgiving across CNN’s global networks. Actress Selena Gomez introduced Ruiz and presented her with the CNN Hero award. Each of the top 10 CNN Heroes also received $25,000.

**Watch Ruiz accept her CNN Hero Award »**

Nominations for the 2009 CNN Heroes opened January 1 and may be submitted at **www.CNN.com/Heroes**.

The Ruiz family’s episode of “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition” is scheduled to air March 15.

EL PASO, Texas (CNN) — For over a dozen years, CNN Hero Maria Ruiz has improved life for children and families in Juarez, Mexico. Recently, however, Ruiz and her own family experienced a dramatic transformation.

As part of ABC’s “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition,” workers prepared to tear down the Ruiz residence and replace it with a specially designed house.

Ruiz had been recognized the previous November during “CNN Heroes: An All-Star Tribute.” The program honored her for traveling across the border from Texas to Juarez several times each week, bringing food, clothing and toys to struggling children and their relatives.

A few months after that recognition, ABC’s home-makeover program surprised Ruiz, her husband and their two children. While the family took a five-day trip to the Bahamas, thousands of volunteers constructed a customized new home for them.

Ruiz recalled the moment host Ty Pennington arrived and called for the family to come outside. They rushed out, stunned that they had been selected. She described the experience as an unexpected and overwhelming blessing.

“Extreme Makeover: Home Edition” chose the Ruiz family from thousands of Texas applicants. According to Pennington, the project was intended not simply to give Ruiz a house, but to provide the resources she needed to expand her efforts. Viewers could also watch the family’s response to their new residence.

Beyond distributing supplies in Juarez, Ruiz and her family have been working to finish a complex in the city that will contain a community kitchen, an orphanage and a vocational school. Additional information about her work was also available.

Ruiz said her family stopped work on its own house in 1996 so they could focus their time on serving the Juarez community. Consequently, numerous sections of the residence remained incomplete. Much of the home’s usable area also became storage space for items donated to families in Juarez.

For Ruiz, a home should provide a place to unwind after a demanding day and allow family members to gather and discuss what happened. That was difficult when donated goods filled the living room.

When the family returned from the Bahamas, thousands of volunteers and local residents welcomed them. The program’s oversized bus initially concealed the renovated property. After the crowd repeated the show’s signature command, “Move that bus!”, the family finally saw its new home.

Ruiz called the house a fresh start that would transform their lives. It would also allow the family to maintain—and potentially increase—its assistance to people in need.

Executive producer Anthony Dominici said the new residence included an extra kitchen as well as additional storage for Ruiz’s charitable work. Community generosity also produced enough food, clothing and toys to pack both a 20-foot shipping container and a 16-foot cube truck. Dominici said the contributions included over 75,000 cans of food.

Pennington explained that the project’s purpose was to make Ruiz’s work easier by supplying what she required to bring hope and dreams to people who had neither.

Ruiz’s mission also centers on educating children so they will eventually serve their own communities. In her view, teaching and preparing children to help others could create a far better world.

Ruiz first gained worldwide attention when “CNN Heroes: An All-Star Tribute” debuted on Thanksgiving across CNN’s global networks. Actress Selena Gomez introduced Ruiz and presented her CNN Hero award. Each of the 10 leading CNN Heroes was also given $25,000, and video of Ruiz accepting the honor was available.

Nominations for the 2009 CNN Heroes program opened on January 1 and could be submitted through www.CNN.com/Heroes.

The Ruiz family’s episode of “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition” was set to broadcast on March 15.

**CNN Hero Maria Ruiz receives life-changing home makeover after years of serving families in Juarez**

*By CNN Staff*

After years spent helping impoverished families in Juarez, Mexico, CNN Hero Maria Ruiz received a life-changing surprise of her own: a custom-built home from ABC’s “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition.”

Ruiz has dedicated much of her life to assisting families facing poverty, hunger and inadequate housing in the border city. Her work has provided support and hope to people navigating difficult circumstances, often requiring her to put the needs of others ahead of her own.

This time, Ruiz was the one surrounded by volunteers eager to help.

The “Extreme Makeover” team designed and built a home tailored to Ruiz and her family, creating a safe, comfortable place where she can rest and continue her humanitarian work. As with the show’s signature projects, the transformation brought together designers, builders and community volunteers in an intensive construction effort.

The emotional reveal marked a rare moment of recognition for Ruiz, whose service has largely focused on people who receive little public attention.

For those familiar with her work, the new home was more than a gift. It was a tribute to years of compassion and sacrifice—and a reminder of the impact one person can have on an entire community.

Ruiz’s story first gained broader attention through CNN Heroes, an initiative honoring everyday people working to improve the lives of others. Her appearance on “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition” brought that mission to a new audience while giving volunteers an opportunity to support the woman who has spent years supporting others.

Standing before the completed house, Ruiz was able to see her own generosity reflected back at her.

The home may have been built in days, but the work it honored was years in the making.

## “Extreme Makeover: Home Edition” and Maria Ruiz’s Work in Juárez

*Extreme Makeover: Home Edition* supported El Paso resident Maria Ruiz not only by replacing her family’s unfinished Texas house, but also by designing the new property around her humanitarian work across the border in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico.

Ruiz regularly collected food, clothing, and household supplies and prepared meals for impoverished families in Juárez. Because the family’s house had never been completed, donated goods competed with everyday living space, while the inadequate kitchen limited how much food she could prepare.

During its rapid rebuild, the program’s design team:

- completed and replaced the family’s unsafe, unfinished home;
- added dedicated storage for donated food, clothing, and other supplies;
- created substantially more kitchen and food-preparation space; and
- separated the family’s living areas from the materials used in Ruiz’s outreach.

The makeover therefore functioned as more than a personal housing gift. By providing a secure place to sort and store donations and a larger kitchen for preparing meals, the program gave Ruiz practical infrastructure to continue—and potentially expand—her charitable service in Juárez while giving her family a stable home.

### From a CNN Stage to a New Front Door, Maria Ruiz’s Family Story Comes Full Circle

Maria Ruiz’s moment in the national spotlight began with an award—but the story behind it was rooted at home.

Honored by CNN Heroes for her service to others, Ruiz received her award from singer and actress Selena Gomez. The presentation celebrated a young person who had turned personal experience into compassion and action, earning recognition far beyond her community.

Yet the ceremony showed only one side of the Ruiz family’s journey. Their everyday struggles—and the close family bond that helped Maria become a young advocate—later reached another national audience when the family appeared on ABC’s *Extreme Makeover: Home Edition*.

The two television moments carried different emotions. The CNN Heroes appearance focused on Maria’s achievements and the people she had helped. *Extreme Makeover* shifted attention to the family behind her, showing how difficult circumstances at home could weigh even on people committed to helping others.

Together, the appearances created an unusually complete portrait. On one stage, Maria stood beside Gomez as an example of youthful generosity. On the other, viewers saw her family receive support from strangers determined to give something back.

For the Ruiz family, the makeover was therefore more than a dramatic renovation and reveal. It was a reminder that heroes can also need help—and that recognizing service means seeing not only the public accomplishment, but also the private sacrifices that made it possible.

Maria’s story connected two programs built around transformation: CNN Heroes honored the change she brought to others, while *Extreme Makeover: Home Edition* helped bring change to her own family.

counterfactuals.output:
## A Home for the Woman Who Gives Everything Away

For years, Maria Ruiz has crossed the Texas–Mexico border carrying more than supplies. With each trip, she has delivered food, clothing and toys to families struggling to meet their most basic needs, offering practical help as well as a reminder that they have not been forgotten.

Ruiz’s humanitarian work grew from a simple desire to serve. She collected donations, organized what she received and transported the goods to communities across the border. Groceries helped families stretch limited budgets. Clothing provided protection and dignity. Toys brought moments of happiness to children whose parents often could not afford presents.

Yet while Ruiz worked to improve life for others, her own home remained unfinished.

The condition of the house reflected the choices she repeatedly made: available time, money and energy went toward her mission instead of her own comfort. Home repairs and construction could wait, she believed, while hungry families and children in need could not. The unfinished rooms became a visible sign of a life in which service consistently came first.

That sacrifice also created practical difficulties. A home that should have been a place of rest had to function as a collection point, sorting area and staging ground for donations. Boxes of food, bags of clothing and toys all required space, making it harder for Ruiz to manage both family life and the growing demands of her outreach.

A television makeover will now give Ruiz something she rarely allowed herself to prioritize: a safe, completed and functional home. But the project’s impact is expected to reach far beyond new walls, furnishings and repairs.

By creating better areas for organizing and storing donated goods, the makeover can help Ruiz operate more efficiently. A stable home base will allow volunteers to sort supplies, prepare shipments and coordinate deliveries with fewer obstacles. It will also give Ruiz the security and breathing room to focus on building partnerships, attracting more donations and reaching additional families on both sides of the border.

Most importantly, the makeover recognizes that supporting a community leader can strengthen the entire community she serves. Ruiz has spent years turning generosity into meals, warm clothes and childhood joy. Now, the television team is helping ensure that the place from which that generosity flows is strong enough to sustain—and expand—her mission.

For Ruiz, the finished home is not simply a reward. It is a new foundation for the work ahead.
